lines.trans: And Arlette, what do we do?
Arlette will understand our choice very well.
And we leave Mathias completely behind?
Mathias does not give moral lessons!
Would the actors follow us?
Of course they are going to follow us.
There is no reason to hesitate.
We must test the waters first.
No, absolutely no testing!
We must not speak of it to anyone.
Otherwise, all of this will leak.
What do we do in that case?
We prepare all the paperwork discreetly.
When everything is ready, we announce everything.
Agreed, so right now, we do it!

examples.text: Ça va? Oui, ça va bien.
examples.trans: How are you? Yes, I'm fine.

meanings.note: ça va? = how are you? / are you okay?

examples.text: Je viens vous annoncer une nouvelle.
examples.trans: I'm coming to announce some news to you.

meanings.note: takes ç before a/o: nous annonçons

examples.text: Il y a un macaron sur la table.
examples.trans: There's a macaron on the table.

meanings.note: elle a quarante ans = she is forty

meanings.en: il y a = there is / there are

meanings.note: as a masculine noun: pour le bien de = for the good of

examples.text: Bien sûr que tu es fatiguée.

meanings.note: bien sûr que + sentence = of course...
en tout cas = in any case, anyway

meanings.en: dans ce cas = in that case

meanings.note: before a noun: ce film, cette tête, ces gens
as a pronoun in c'est, ce n'est pas; becomes c' before a vowel
cela ne change rien = that changes nothing

examples.text: Gardez cela pour vous, s'il vous plaît.
Cela ne change rien au projet.
examples.trans: That changes nothing about the project.

examples.text: Je peux te voir seul d'abord?

meanings.note: dans une heure = in an hour

examples.text: La plus grande imprésario de Paris.

examples.text: Bien sûr, nous respectons votre démarche.
examples.trans: Of course, we respect your approach.
It is a very original approach.

meanings.note: preposition: en vacances, en huit ans
pronoun before the verb: j'en ai assez, je n'en peux plus

examples.text: Est-ce que j'ai fait quelque chose de mal?

meanings.en: turns a sentence into a yes/no question
meanings.note: est-ce que tu viens? = are you coming?
pour faire quoi? = to do what?
faire du vélo = to ride a bike, to cycle

falloir.governs: il faut + infinitive, or il faut que + subjunctive

meanings.en: lesson, educational instruction or piece of advice

tag at the end of a question
everyday speech, with a he/she verb form

tu viens quand? = when are you coming?

examples.trans: Otherwise, I'll look for a job at another agency.
